question: Should OpenClaw standardize on roots/access modes, allow/deny rules, or a narrower combined `tools.fs` contract, and should v1 explicitly exclude arbitrary exec-mediated filesystem access?
rationale: This determines a public configuration API and the strength of a security guarantee; the competing open PRs cannot safely resolve that product and security decision mechanically.

options.title: Narrow combined tools.fs v1
options.body: Specify managed file and media roots with deny-wins exceptions under `tools.fs`, explicitly exclude arbitrary exec, and require one candidate PR to conform.

options.title: Adopt roots/access modes
options.body: Sponsor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/52951 after resolving its compatibility, conflict, and remaining review state.

options.title: Adopt PathGuard allow/deny
options.body: Sponsor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/60981 after adding real behavior proof, resolving conflicts, and reducing unrelated session and configuration scope.

recommendation.title: Narrow combined tools.fs v1
recommendation.body: Specify managed file and media roots with deny-wins exceptions under `tools.fs`, explicitly exclude arbitrary exec, and require one candidate PR to conform.
